newsitem.title: USA: Democrats to scrutinize EPA air proposal-US sen.
newsitem.headline: Democrats to scrutinize EPA air proposal-US sen.

text.p: A number of Senate Democrats are likely to challenge a proposal to tighten air quality standards unless the Clinton administration can make a clear scientific case for the change, Sen. John Breaux, a Louisiana Democrat, said Wednesday.
"More members are not willing to accept this without challenging it," Breaux said at a National Association of Manufacturers conference.
Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Carol Browner will discuss the agency's controversial proposal Thursday before the Senate Democratic Caucus, Breaux said.
Breaux said he did not think Browner so far has made an adequate scientific argument for the stricter standards against smog and soot, and said the scientific community was divided on the issue.
"With as much disagreement as I've heard it doesnt seem to me it justifies a policy being changed based on unclear science," he said.
Breaux said he has raised concerns on the proposal to President Clinton and the Office of Management and Budget, and the proposal "is not going to slip through unchallenged."
The EPA is to announce its final decision on the new standards in July, and Browner has said repeatedly she has not made up her mind on the issue.
Breaux said it is a tough issue in Louisiana, with an economy heavily depending on the petro-chemical industry.
"People want clean air, but they also want jobs and industry," he said.

Breaux's comments came after 42 House Democrats -- mostly from the industrial Ohio Valley and Great Lakes regions -- in a letter this week also urged the Clintion administration to rethink the air quality proposal.

Breaux said he did not think the Senate was as focused on yet on the issue as the House, where he said the issue has been highlighted by a split between key Democrats Henry Waxman of California, who supports the proposal, and John Dingell of Michigan, who opposes it.
